subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: Should stale PTY-backed background exec runs from a previous gateway epoch be killed on startup, or reattached/re-registered as live process sessions?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the ownership gap, but choosing kill versus reattach changes operator semantics for legitimate long-running work and needs maintainer intent before a durable fix lands.

options.title: Kill stale startup orphans
options.body: On gateway startup, use durable PTY exec records to terminate previous-epoch process trees that OpenClaw cannot safely own anymore, favoring availability and predictable cleanup.

options.title: Reattach previous-epoch runs
options.body: Persist enough metadata to rebuild process sessions after restart, preserving long-running work but accepting a more complex ownership and security model.

options.title: Land only in-process reconciliation
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/66001 as a scoped mitigation and keep a separate issue for cold-start orphan reaping.

recommendation.title: Kill stale startup orphans
recommendation.body: On gateway startup, use durable PTY exec records to terminate previous-epoch process trees that OpenClaw cannot safely own anymore, favoring availability and predictable cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main and release provenance makes this the best available owner for a release-sensitive process lifecycle choice.
